params.text: Core: 10 routers, one address each (203.0.113.1 to .10, in the order listed). Cables have no length of their own, so each takes the distance between the two cities it joins.

EU side: gw-eu is 198.51.100.1 behind madrid, LAN 192.168.10.0/24. host-eu holds 192.168.10.3 and gen-eu shares its hub. gen-eu sends two random frames of about 1KiB, back to back, under host-eu's address and hardware address: a gateway translates what comes from its own LAN and nothing else, so that is what gets them out. Its NAT forwards UDP port 5000 to host-eu, as gw-us does to host-us, so either host is reachable from the other at its gateway's public address.

US side: gw-us is 198.51.100.2 behind los-angeles, LAN 192.168.20.0/24. Its NAT forwards UDP port 5000 to host-us, which is what the frames from gen-eu are addressed to; without that they would go no further than the gateway. hub-us sits between host-us and gw-us so that rec-us sees everything either of them says, and writes it into /tmp/packet-pair.pcap.
